source.title: Understanding the role of individual units in a deep neural network
source.authors: David Bau; Jun-Yan Zhu; Hendrik Strobelt; Àgata Lapedriza; Bo-Lei Zhou; A. Torralba

record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes semantic matches and causal roles of units, but does not measure whether individual units respond to several unrelated inputs.
record.gate_note: The paper reports unit-to-concept matches and tests one airplane unit on a separate object-image dataset. These results concern unit interpretability, but its method assigns each unit its highest-scoring concept and does not report whether a unit also matches unrelated concepts. Unit-removal and GAN-intervention results concern causal roles, not polysemanticity; cited results are not included.
record.test_reason: Network dissection assigns each unit its single best-matching concept and reports counts of matched concepts. It never measures whether a unit responds to several unrelated inputs, so it does not test any version of polysemanticity. It only notes that some units are less interpretable by IoU.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is essentially right. Network dissection finds many interpretable units in supervised classifiers and unsupervised GANs. Ablation and activation show these units play causal roles: decomposing scene classification into object sub-problems, and rendering objects context-sensitively. This enables understanding of adversarial attacks and semantic image editing.
record.recipe_differences: Uses network dissection, matching unit activations to segmented concepts and measuring intervention effects; it does not use the original claim's cited methods to quantify polysemanticity.

fits_no_version.finding: Units in a Places365 VGG-16 and a Progressive GAN match human-interpretable concepts. The most interpretable units (by IoU) are important to many output classes; units important to one or no class are less interpretable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In trained image networks, many individual units match single human-interpretable concepts, and unit interpretability correlates with importance across output classes.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
record.problems: The concept-matching analysis assigns each unit its highest-scoring concept and reports thresholded matches; it does not establish whether units also respond to other unrelated concepts. The reported unit-to-concept counts therefore cannot determine polysemanticity.
record.rows_left_out: Unit-removal, GAN unit-intervention, adversarial-attack, and semantic-editing outcomes were left out because they measure causal roles or application behavior rather than whether units respond to unrelated inputs.

untested.parts: Whether classifier units respond strongly to multiple unrelated concepts. Only each unit's top concept is reported.
Superposition and capacity pressure are not examined.
Origins of polysemanticity without capacity pressure are not examined.
No comparison of polysemanticity across activation functions or architectures is made in the main text. AlexNet and ResNet comparisons are only in the SI and concern interpretability counts.
Not tested whether apparently mixed units share one feature.
Only the top 1% activation threshold with IoU scoring is used. The authors do not vary it to test effects on polysemanticity judgments.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T6/discusses assignment and its exclusion of ablation and intervention results are appropriate. The paper's remark that the method 'relies on the emergence of disentangled' units is relevant context but is not a measurement of polysemanticity.

versions.untested_parts: Whether individual classifier neurons respond strongly to multiple unrelated inputs.
Superposition, feature sparsity, and capacity pressure.
Polysemanticity from initialization, regularization, or training noise without capacity pressure.
Comparisons of activation functions, architectures, or regularization for polysemanticity.
Whether purportedly unrelated mixtures share a feature or job.
Whether polysemanticity judgments change across activation ranges or explanation scores.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Matched unit activations to segmented visual concepts using IoU; reported concepts with IoU ratio at least 4%.
rows.measure: Number of distinct concepts matched by units, by category
rows.value: 51 object classes, 22 parts, 12 materials, and 8 colors
rows.locator: Results, Emergence of Object Detectors in a Scene Classifier; Figure 1
rows.note: Counts are aggregates of unit-to-concept matches; the study labels each unit by its highest-scoring concept and does not report multiple unrelated matches per unit.
rows.check: Count of best-match concepts across units. This is not a per-unit test of multiple unrelated responses. The link to none is correct.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Matched unit activations to segmented visual concepts using IoU.
rows.measure: Number of concepts matched by units, by category
rows.value: 28 object classes, 25 parts, 9 materials, and 8 colors
rows.locator: Results, Emergence of Object Detectors in a Scene Classifier; Figure 1
rows.note: The paper reports these category counts for conv5_1; it does not report how many unrelated concepts any one unit matches.
rows.check: Same as R1, for conv5_1. The link to none is correct.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated unit 150 as an airplane classifier on ImageNet using a peak-activation threshold.

conditions.value: ImageNet; images and classes disjoint from Places365 training set

rows.measure: Balanced accuracy distinguishing the two airplane classes from other object classes
rows.locator: Results, Emergence of Object Detectors in a Scene Classifier; Figure 1f
rows.note: This evaluates the unit's airplane-detection performance, not whether it also responds to unrelated concepts.
rows.check: Selectivity of a single airplane unit (85.6% balanced accuracy). It does not report what else the unit responds to.

rows.subject: Progressive GAN
rows.operation_detail: Matched unit activations to segmented visual concepts using IoU.
rows.measure: Number of unit matches, by concept category
rows.value: 19 object-specific units, 41 units matching object parts, one material, and six color units
rows.locator: Results, Emergence of Object Detectors in a GAN; Figure 3
rows.note: This is a generative model, not a classifier; the reported counts do not assess multiple unrelated concepts per unit.
rows.check: GAN generator, not a classifier. These are counts of unit-to-concept matches.
